Introduction

Los Angeles businesses face some of the highest commercial electricity rates in California, making energy efficiency more critical than ever. One of the fastest, most cost-effective ways to reduce operating expenses is through an LED lighting retrofit. At Shaffer Construction, we've helped hundreds of Los Angeles businesses slash their energy bills by 40-60% through strategic LED upgrades, with many clients seeing full return on investment in less than two years.

This comprehensive guide covers everything Los Angeles business owners need to know about LED retrofits: detailed cost-benefit analysis, current LADWP rebate programs with specific incentive amounts, federal tax deductions, the installation process, and long-term maintenance benefits. Whether you operate an office building, warehouse, retail space, or parking facility, upgrading to LED lighting is one of the smartest investments you can make for your bottom line.

Understanding LED Retrofit: What It Is and Why It Matters

An LED retrofit involves replacing your existing lighting fixtures or bulbs with energy-efficient LED technology. Unlike a complete lighting system overhaul, a retrofit works with your current infrastructure, making it a faster and more affordable upgrade path. For Los Angeles businesses, this typically means converting fluorescent tubes, metal halide fixtures, or halogen lights to modern LED equivalents.

The business case for LED retrofits has never been stronger. LED technology has matured significantly over the past decade, with prices dropping while performance and efficiency have improved dramatically. Today's commercial LED fixtures produce superior light quality, last 25,000-50,000 hours compared to just 7,000-15,000 hours for fluorescent bulbs, and consume 40-75% less electricity than traditional lighting technologies.

For Los Angeles businesses specifically, LED retrofits address several critical concerns: reducing high LADWP electricity costs, meeting California's strict Title 24 energy codes, improving workplace safety and productivity through better lighting quality, and demonstrating corporate commitment to sustainability. With generous rebates from LADWP and substantial federal tax incentives, the financial barriers to upgrading have been virtually eliminated.

Cost-Benefit Analysis: Calculating Your LED Retrofit ROI

Understanding the return on investment for an LED retrofit requires looking at both upfront costs and ongoing savings. The typical commercial LED retrofit project in Los Angeles ranges from $2,000 to $50,000+ depending on facility size and complexity, but the energy and maintenance savings often deliver payback periods of just 6 months to 2 years.

Let's examine a real-world example: A 10,000 square foot Los Angeles office building with 100 fluorescent fixtures operating 12 hours per day. The existing fluorescent fixtures consume approximately 40 watts each (4,000 total watts), while equivalent LED fixtures consume just 18 watts each (1,800 total watts). At Los Angeles commercial electricity rates averaging $0.20 per kilowatt-hour, here's the financial breakdown:

Annual Energy Consumption - Fluorescent: 100 fixtures × 40 watts × 4,380 hours per year ÷ 1,000 = 17,520 kWh. Annual cost: $3,504.

Annual Energy Consumption - LED: 100 fixtures × 18 watts × 4,380 hours per year ÷ 1,000 = 7,884 kWh. Annual cost: $1,577.

Annual Energy Savings: $1,927 per year (55% reduction).

Beyond energy savings, LED retrofits deliver substantial maintenance cost reductions. Fluorescent bulbs require replacement every 2-3 years in commercial settings, while LEDs last 10-15 years or longer. For a facility with 100 fixtures, this means avoiding approximately $500-800 annually in replacement bulb costs and labor. When you combine $1,927 in energy savings with $650 in maintenance savings (conservatively), the total annual savings reach $2,577.

If the LED retrofit costs $20,000 installed, the simple payback period is 7.8 years without incentives. However, with LADWP rebates potentially covering 30-50% of costs and federal Section 179D deductions providing additional tax benefits, the effective out-of-pocket cost might drop to $10,000-12,000, reducing payback to just 3.9-4.7 years. Many Los Angeles businesses report even faster payback periods, especially those operating extended hours or with aging, inefficient legacy lighting systems.

LADWP Commercial Lighting Rebate Programs

The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power offers one of the most generous commercial lighting incentive programs in California through its Commercial Lighting Incentive Program (CLIP). These rebates can dramatically reduce the upfront cost of LED retrofits, making projects financially viable that might otherwise have marginal economics.

CLIP Incentive Structure: LADWP provides incentives based on calculated energy savings, with rates ranging from $0.08 to $0.40 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) of annualized savings. This performance-based approach rewards projects that deliver the greatest energy reductions. Remarkably, some projects may qualify for incentives covering up to 100% of project costs, though 30-50% coverage is more typical for standard LED retrofit projects.

Eligibility Requirements: To qualify for CLIP rebates, your business must be a LADWP commercial customer in good standing with current monthly electrical demand greater than 200 kW (indicated as "Facilities Charge" on your bill). All lighting equipment must be listed on the Design Lights Consortium's (DLC) Qualified Products List to ensure quality and performance standards. Most importantly, you must receive LADWP approval before starting work or purchasing equipment, as retroactive rebates are not available.

Application Process: The CLIP application process begins with a pre-approval application submitted to LADWP before any work commences. Shaffer Construction handles the entire rebate application process for our clients, including energy calculations, equipment documentation, and post-installation verification. LADWP typically processes applications within 2-4 weeks, and rebate payments are issued after final inspection confirms proper installation.

Additional LADWP Programs: Beyond CLIP, LADWP offers the Custom Performance Program for larger, more complex energy efficiency projects. This program can combine lighting upgrades with HVAC improvements, building envelope enhancements, and other efficiency measures for comprehensive facility upgrades with even more substantial incentives. LADWP also hosts regular workshops and open houses throughout 2025 to help businesses understand available programs and maximize incentive opportunities.

Federal Tax Incentives: Section 179D Deduction

The federal Section 179D Commercial Buildings Energy Efficiency Tax Deduction provides substantial tax benefits for businesses investing in energy-efficient lighting systems. This powerful incentive can deliver immediate tax savings that further accelerate LED retrofit payback periods.

2025 Deduction Amounts: Under current law, Section 179D allows commercial building owners to claim up to $5.81 per square foot in tax deductions for qualifying energy-efficient improvements, including LED lighting systems. The exact deduction amount depends on the energy savings achieved and whether the project meets prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements.

For projects meeting prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements, the minimum deduction is $2.50 per square foot for achieving 25% energy savings compared to ASHRAE 90.1 baseline standards, scaling up to a maximum of $5.00 per square foot for higher efficiency levels. For projects not meeting these labor requirements, deductions range from $0.50 to $1.00 per square foot, which is still significant but substantially lower.

Lighting-Specific Qualifications: LED lighting retrofits can qualify for Section 179D deductions when the new system reduces lighting power density by at least 25% compared to ASHRAE 90.1 standards. Many modern LED retrofits easily exceed this threshold, with 40-60% reductions being common. The deduction applies to interior lighting systems, including controls and sensors that reduce energy consumption.

Real-World Example: A 20,000 square foot Los Angeles warehouse completing an LED retrofit that achieves 50% energy savings could potentially claim a $2.50-5.00 per square foot deduction (depending on wage requirements), resulting in $50,000-100,000 in tax deductions. For a business with a 25% effective tax rate, this translates to $12,500-25,000 in actual tax savings, further reducing the net cost of the lighting upgrade.

Important Deadline: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act added a critical termination provision: Section 179D shall not apply to property where construction begins after June 30, 2026. Los Angeles businesses considering LED retrofits should plan to begin their projects before this deadline to capture these valuable tax benefits. Shaffer Construction works with qualified energy professionals to ensure all Section 179D documentation requirements are met for maximum tax benefit.

LED vs. Traditional Lighting: A Comprehensive Cost Comparison

To fully appreciate the value of LED retrofits, it's essential to understand how LED technology compares to traditional lighting options across all cost factors: energy consumption, lifespan, maintenance requirements, and light quality.

Energy Consumption Comparison: LED lights consume 40-75% less electricity than comparable traditional lighting technologies. A 4-foot LED tube replacement consumes approximately 18 watts compared to 32-40 watts for a T8 fluorescent tube, representing a 55-60% reduction. When compared to older T12 fluorescent technology still found in many Los Angeles buildings, LEDs use up to 75% less energy. Metal halide fixtures common in warehouses and parking lots consume 150-400 watts, while LED equivalents deliver the same light output at just 50-150 watts.

Lifespan and Replacement Frequency: LED fixtures last 25,000-50,000 hours in typical commercial applications, compared to 7,000-15,000 hours for fluorescent tubes, 2,000-4,000 hours for halogen bulbs, and 10,000-20,000 hours for metal halide lamps. In practical terms, an LED fixture operating 12 hours daily will last 6-11 years before requiring replacement, while fluorescent tubes need replacement every 2-3 years. This extended lifespan dramatically reduces maintenance labor costs, especially in facilities with high ceilings or difficult-to-access fixtures.

Total Cost of Ownership: While LED fixtures cost more upfront (typically $30-150 per fixture vs. $10-30 for fluorescent), the total cost of ownership over a 10-year period heavily favors LEDs. A University of Michigan study found that LED lighting is up to 44% more cost-effective than fluorescent tubes when accounting for all factors. For Los Angeles businesses, monthly electricity savings of 10-20% from lighting upgrades alone are common, with payback periods under 6 months reported for facilities with extensive operating hours.

Light Quality and Performance: Modern LEDs offer superior color rendering (CRI of 80-90+ vs. 60-75 for fluorescent), instant-on operation without warm-up periods, better performance in cold temperatures, and no flicker or hum. These quality improvements translate to enhanced workplace safety, improved employee productivity, and better customer experiences in retail environments. Studies consistently show that better lighting quality reduces workplace errors and accidents while increasing employee satisfaction.

Types of Commercial LED Retrofits in Los Angeles

Different business environments have unique lighting needs and retrofit opportunities. Understanding the specific considerations for your facility type helps optimize your LED retrofit strategy and maximize returns.

Office Buildings: Los Angeles office retrofits typically focus on replacing fluorescent troffer fixtures in drop ceilings with LED panels or retrofit kits. Modern LED office lighting delivers 90+ lumens per watt efficiency while providing excellent color rendering for computer work. Smart controls including occupancy sensors, daylight harvesting, and dimming capabilities can boost energy savings by an additional 20-30% beyond fixture upgrades alone. For a typical 10,000 square foot office, LED retrofits cost $15,000-35,000 but deliver $2,000-4,000 in annual savings.

Warehouses and Distribution Centers: High-bay LED fixtures have revolutionized warehouse lighting, replacing inefficient metal halide and high-pressure sodium fixtures that consume 250-400 watts each. Modern LED high-bay fixtures deliver equivalent or superior illumination at just 90-150 watts while turning on instantly (eliminating the 10-15 minute warm-up period of metal halide). For a 50,000 square foot warehouse with 100 high-bay fixtures, retrofits typically cost $30,000-60,000 but can save $8,000-15,000 annually. The instant-on capability also improves safety by eliminating dim periods after power interruptions.

Parking Lots and Garages: Outdoor lighting retrofits address both energy costs and safety concerns. LED parking lot fixtures and pole lights consume 50-70% less energy than metal halide or high-pressure sodium fixtures while providing better light distribution and color rendering. LED garage lighting improves security and surveillance camera performance while reducing maintenance in difficult-to-access locations. Parking structure retrofits often qualify for enhanced LADWP incentives due to substantial energy savings potential.

Retail Spaces: Retail LED retrofits focus on creating attractive, inviting environments while reducing operating costs. Track lighting, display lighting, and general illumination can all be upgraded to LED technology. High-CRI LEDs (90+) accurately render merchandise colors, critical for clothing, cosmetics, and food retailers. Dimming capabilities allow retailers to adjust lighting for different times of day and create desired atmospheres. Retail retrofits typically cost $3,000-15,000 for small to medium locations, with savings of $500-2,500 annually plus reduced heat load decreasing air conditioning costs.

The LED Retrofit Installation Process

Understanding the installation process helps Los Angeles businesses plan effectively and minimize operational disruption. Shaffer Construction has refined a systematic approach that ensures quality results while keeping your business running smoothly.

Phase 1: Initial Assessment and Energy Audit (1-2 weeks): Our licensed electricians conduct a comprehensive lighting audit, documenting existing fixtures, measuring light levels, calculating current energy consumption, and identifying safety issues or code violations. We evaluate your facility's specific needs, operating hours, and lighting requirements to develop a customized retrofit strategy. This assessment forms the basis for accurate energy savings calculations required for LADWP rebate applications and Section 179D documentation.

Phase 2: Design and Proposal Development (1 week): We design a lighting solution that balances performance, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. This includes selecting DLC-qualified LED fixtures appropriate for your applications, specifying controls and sensors to maximize savings, and creating photometric layouts ensuring proper illumination levels. Our detailed proposals include equipment specifications, installation scope, project timeline, total costs, and projected savings including applicable rebates and tax incentives.

Phase 3: Rebate Application and Permitting (2-4 weeks): Before any work begins, we submit pre-approval applications to LADWP's CLIP program with all required documentation. Simultaneously, we obtain necessary electrical permits from the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety. This concurrent process minimizes delays. LADWP typically reviews applications within 2-4 weeks, after which we receive authorization to proceed with the project.

Phase 4: Equipment Procurement (1-3 weeks): Once approvals are secured, we order all fixtures, controls, and materials. Lead times vary based on product availability and project size, but standard commercial LED fixtures typically ship within 1-2 weeks. For large projects requiring custom specifications or substantial quantities, procurement may take 3-4 weeks.

Phase 5: Installation (1-5 days): The actual installation timeline depends on facility size and complexity. A typical office retrofit with 50-100 fixtures takes 2-3 days, while large warehouse projects may require a week. We work during evenings, weekends, or in phases to minimize disruption to your business operations. Our installation process includes safe removal of old fixtures, proper disposal of ballasts and tubes (including any hazardous materials), installation of new LED fixtures, integration of controls and sensors, testing and commissioning all systems, and final cleanup with complete debris removal.

Phase 6: Inspection and Verification (1-2 weeks): After installation completion, Los Angeles building inspectors verify all work meets electrical code requirements. LADWP also conducts post-installation verification for rebate purposes, confirming that approved equipment was properly installed. This typically occurs within 1-2 weeks of project completion.

Phase 7: Final Documentation and Rebate Processing (2-6 weeks): We compile all documentation for LADWP rebate payment and Section 179D tax deduction support. LADWP processes final rebate payments typically within 4-6 weeks of verification. We provide you with complete documentation including as-built drawings, equipment specifications and warranties, energy savings reports, and tax documentation for Section 179D deductions.

Total timeline from initial assessment to rebate payment typically ranges from 8-16 weeks, with the most time-intensive phases being permitting, equipment procurement, and rebate processing rather than the actual installation work.

Maintenance Benefits and Long-Term Lifespan

One of the most compelling but often overlooked advantages of LED retrofits is the dramatic reduction in ongoing maintenance requirements. For Los Angeles businesses, this translates to substantial labor savings and improved operational reliability.

Extended Replacement Intervals: With rated lifespans of 25,000-50,000 hours, LED fixtures operating 12 hours daily will last 6-11 years before requiring replacement. This stands in stark contrast to fluorescent tubes needing replacement every 2-3 years, halogen bulbs every 1-2 years, and metal halide lamps every 2-4 years. For a facility with 200 fixtures, eliminating 2-3 replacement cycles over a decade saves substantial labor costs, especially in warehouses with 30-foot ceilings requiring lift equipment for access.

Reduced Emergency Lighting Failures: LED reliability significantly reduces unexpected lighting failures that create safety hazards and require emergency service calls. Traditional lighting technologies experience increasing failure rates as they age, while LEDs maintain consistent performance throughout their lifespan before gradually dimming near end-of-life. This predictable degradation pattern allows planned replacement scheduling rather than reactive emergency repairs.

Lower HVAC Costs: LEDs generate significantly less heat than traditional lighting, reducing cooling loads in Los Angeles's warm climate. For every watt of lighting power reduced, air conditioning requirements drop by approximately 0.25-0.35 watts. A retrofit reducing lighting power by 10 kilowatts could decrease cooling loads by 2.5-3.5 kilowatts, saving an additional $500-1,000 annually in warm Los Angeles summers. This secondary benefit often goes uncounted in standard ROI calculations but provides real operational savings.

Simplified Inventory Management: Standardizing on LED technology eliminates the need to stock multiple bulb types, ballasts, and starters. Many businesses maintain expensive inventories of 5-10 different bulb types for their various fixtures. LED retrofits allow consolidation to just 2-3 LED fixture types, reducing inventory carrying costs and simplifying maintenance procedures.

Performance Consistency: Unlike fluorescent and HID lighting that degrades noticeably over time (often losing 20-30% of initial light output before failure), LEDs maintain 70% or more of their initial output throughout their rated lifespan. This consistent performance means you don't experience the gradual darkening that forces premature replacement of traditional bulbs, further extending effective lifespan and reducing total ownership costs.

Environmental and Sustainability Benefits

Beyond financial returns, LED retrofits deliver substantial environmental benefits that align with Los Angeles's aggressive climate action goals and corporate sustainability commitments.

Carbon Emissions Reduction: LADWP's energy mix includes both renewable and fossil fuel sources. Every kilowatt-hour saved through LED efficiency reduces carbon emissions associated with electricity generation. A typical commercial LED retrofit saving 50,000 kWh annually prevents approximately 15-20 metric tons of CO2 emissions per year—equivalent to taking 3-4 cars off the road. Over a 10-year period, a single retrofit project can eliminate 150-200 tons of carbon emissions.

Mercury Elimination: Fluorescent tubes contain 3-5 milligrams of mercury each, requiring special disposal procedures and creating environmental hazards if broken. A business using 500 fluorescent tubes will dispose of approximately 1,000-1,500 tubes over a decade, releasing 3-7 grams of mercury into the waste stream. LED technology contains no mercury or other hazardous materials, simplifying disposal and eliminating this environmental concern entirely.

Reduced Resource Consumption: The 10-15 year lifespan of LED fixtures means manufacturing fewer replacement products compared to traditional lighting requiring replacement every 2-3 years. This reduces raw material consumption, manufacturing energy, packaging waste, and transportation emissions associated with producing and distributing replacement bulbs. Over a decade, a 200-fixture facility will consume 200 LED fixtures versus 600-1,000 fluorescent tubes—a 67-80% reduction in product consumption.

Supporting California Climate Goals: California has committed to carbon neutrality by 2045, with interim goals including 100% clean electricity by 2045. Energy efficiency through LED retrofits helps businesses contribute to these statewide objectives while reducing grid strain during peak demand periods. Los Angeles businesses that document energy efficiency improvements can leverage these achievements in corporate sustainability reporting, ESG disclosures, and green building certifications like LEED.

Light Pollution Reduction: Modern LED fixtures with proper shielding and directional optics reduce light trespass and sky glow compared to older fixtures. This is particularly important for parking lot and exterior lighting retrofits, where improved optical control directs light where needed rather than scattering into the night sky. Reduced light pollution benefits local ecosystems while maintaining superior safety and security illumination.

Smart Controls and Advanced LED Systems

While basic LED retrofits deliver substantial savings, integrating smart controls and advanced management systems can increase energy savings by an additional 20-40% beyond fixture upgrades alone.

Occupancy Sensors: Automatically turning lights off in unoccupied spaces prevents the waste of lighting empty offices, conference rooms, restrooms, and warehouse areas. Studies show that occupancy sensors typically reduce lighting energy consumption by 20-30% in spaces with intermittent use. For Los Angeles office buildings, sensor-controlled lighting in private offices and conference rooms delivers quick payback while improving convenience.

Daylight Harvesting: Photosensors detect available natural light and automatically dim artificial lighting to maintain consistent illumination levels. In Los Angeles's sunny climate, perimeter offices and spaces with skylights receive substantial natural light during daytime hours. Daylight harvesting systems can reduce lighting energy by 30-50% in these areas while maintaining optimal light levels throughout the day. This technology particularly benefits retail spaces and offices with extensive window area.

Dimming and Tuning: LED technology supports smooth dimming from 100% to 10% or lower without the flickering or reduced lifespan issues of fluorescent dimming. Businesses can implement time-based dimming schedules that reduce lighting levels during low-activity periods like evening cleaning shifts. Some advanced systems even support color temperature tuning, adjusting from cool white (5000K) during active work hours to warm white (3000K) during evening hours, aligning with natural circadian rhythms and potentially improving employee wellbeing.

Centralized Management Systems: Networked lighting control systems allow facility managers to monitor, control, and optimize lighting across entire buildings or multi-site portfolios from centralized dashboards. These systems provide real-time energy consumption data, identify malfunctioning fixtures before they fail completely, generate compliance reports for energy audits, and enable remote troubleshooting and adjustment. For Los Angeles businesses with multiple locations, centralized control reduces management complexity while maximizing efficiency.

Integration with Building Management Systems: Advanced LED control systems integrate with BMS platforms, coordinating lighting with HVAC, security, and other building systems. This integration enables sophisticated strategies like reducing lighting and HVAC in unoccupied zones, adjusting lighting based on security system status, and optimizing total building energy consumption during demand response events. Such integration represents the future of commercial building efficiency and can unlock additional utility incentives through LADWP's Custom Performance Program.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to see return on investment from an LED retrofit?

Most Los Angeles businesses see full ROI within 1-3 years depending on operating hours, electricity rates, and available incentives. Facilities operating extended hours (16+ hours daily) often achieve payback in under 12 months. With LADWP rebates covering 30-50% of costs and Section 179D tax deductions providing additional benefits, effective payback periods frequently drop to 6-18 months. Warehouses and facilities with expensive-to-maintain high-bay lighting see the fastest returns.

Can we complete the retrofit in phases to spread out costs?

Yes, phased retrofits are common and often practical for larger facilities. Many businesses start with the highest-use areas or least efficient fixtures to maximize immediate savings, then use those energy cost reductions to fund subsequent phases. LADWP's CLIP program accepts phased applications, allowing you to secure rebates for each phase independently. Shaffer Construction can develop a multi-year master plan that prioritizes areas by ROI while maintaining consistent lighting quality throughout your facility.

Will LED retrofits work with our existing fixtures and wiring?

In most cases, yes. LED retrofit kits and bulbs are available for nearly all common commercial fixture types, including fluorescent troffers, high-bay fixtures, wall packs, and parking lot lights. Some retrofits simply replace bulbs and bypass ballasts, while others replace entire fixture housings. Our initial assessment determines the most cost-effective approach for your specific fixtures. Existing wiring typically remains serviceable since LEDs draw less current than the fixtures they replace.

How do LADWP rebates work and how long does it take to receive payment?

LADWP's CLIP program requires pre-approval before starting work. We submit your application with energy calculations and equipment specifications. Once approved (typically 2-4 weeks), we complete the installation. After final inspection, LADWP verifies proper installation and processes rebate payment, usually within 4-6 weeks. Total timeline from application to payment ranges from 8-12 weeks. Rebates are paid as checks or credits to your LADWP account based on your preference.

What happens to our old fluorescent tubes and ballasts?

Shaffer Construction handles all disposal in compliance with California hazardous waste regulations. Fluorescent tubes containing mercury must be recycled through certified facilities—we never send them to standard landfills. We transport all old fixtures, tubes, and ballasts to appropriate recycling or disposal facilities and provide documentation of proper disposal for your environmental compliance records. This service is included in our project pricing.

Can LED lighting improve employee productivity and safety?

Research consistently shows that better lighting quality enhances workplace performance. LEDs provide superior color rendering (making colors appear more natural), eliminate flicker that causes eye strain and headaches, and deliver consistent light levels without the gradual dimming of aging fluorescent tubes. Warehouse studies document 10-20% reductions in picking errors after LED upgrades. Office workers report less eye strain and fatigue. Better illuminated parking areas and exterior spaces demonstrably improve security and reduce accidents.

Do LED retrofits qualify for green building certifications?

Yes, LED lighting upgrades contribute points toward LEED certification, ENERGY STAR certification for buildings, and other green building programs. The energy savings, reduced environmental impact, and improved light quality all support certification requirements. We provide complete documentation of energy reductions, materials specifications, and performance data needed for certification applications. For Los Angeles businesses pursuing sustainability certifications, LED retrofits represent one of the most straightforward and cost-effective strategies for earning points.

Conclusion

LED retrofits represent one of the highest-return investments available to Los Angeles businesses today. With energy savings of 40-75%, maintenance cost reductions of 50-80%, and payback periods as short as 6-18 months when incentives are maximized, the financial case is compelling. LADWP's generous rebate programs covering up to 50% of project costs combined with federal Section 179D tax deductions of $2.50-5.00 per square foot make LED retrofits more accessible than ever.

Beyond the impressive financial returns, LED retrofits deliver improved lighting quality that enhances employee productivity and safety, dramatic reductions in environmental impact supporting corporate sustainability goals, and simplified maintenance reducing operational complexity. For Los Angeles businesses facing high electricity costs and increasing pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, LED retrofits check every box.

The window for maximum incentives is limited, with Section 179D deductions scheduled to expire for projects beginning after June 30, 2026. Los Angeles businesses should act now to secure these valuable benefits while they remain available.
